pr_title: Support calling EVP_DigestUpdate instead of EVP_Digest[Sign|Verify]Update
pr_body:
Prior to OpenSSL 3.0 EVP_Digest[Sign|Verify|Update were just macros for
EVP_DigestUpdate. They are now separate functions. Unfortunately some
code assumes that EVP_Digest[Sign|Verify]Update is interchangeable with
EVP_DigestUpdate. For example the dgst app uses an MD bio which always
calls EVP_DigestUpdate(). However the dgst app supports signing instead
of digesting and may initialise with EVP_DigestSignInit_ex() instead of
just EVP_DigestInit().

We now detect these differences and redirect to the correct function
where appropriate.

Fixes #10114

A secondary issue related to #10114 is that the implementation of the MD BIO used internal EVP_MD_CTX knowledge that hadn't been updated with knowledge about providers. There's really no reason for that code to use internal knowledge so instead we use the public APIs.

issue_context.title: EVP_DigestUpdate crashes with dgst command-line
issue_context.body:
Hey OpenSSL team, our [Triggerflow](https://gitlab.com/nisec/openssl-triggerflow-ci/pipelines) tool detected a [problem](https://gitlab.com/nisec/openssl-triggerflow-ci/-/jobs/310739852) during some of our testing in master.

Further inspection it seems that `EVP_DigestUpdate` crashes when using the dgst command-line tool to generate DSA signatures. For example,
```
openssl dgst -sha512 -sign dsa.pem -out lsb-release.sig data
```

I believe the issue is in a NULL pointer indirection in `EVP_DigestUpdate`. 
```
legacy:
    return ctx->update(ctx, data, count);
```

### gdb output
```
(gdb) p *ctx
$1 = {reqdigest = 0x7ffff785c520 <sha512_md>, digest = 0x0, engine = 0x0, flags = 0, md_data = 0x0, pctx = 0x55555584c830, update = 0x0, provctx = 0x0, fetched_digest = 0x0}
```

We appreciate if you could take a look into this.
